target_customer: Advertisers and publishers running tablet-optimized ad campaigns
problem: Ads on tablets were mostly shrunk phone or desktop formats; advertisers and publishers lacked tools to collaborate on touch-friendly ads.
business_model: Advertising technology platform; pricing not found

founders.name: Matt Holden
founders.background_notes: YC bio also lists Whywhywhy as a later venture. Dates of the Dropbox and Google roles are not on the page.

founders.name: Sean Lynch
founders.background_notes: YC page lists his focus as data and APIs; no bio.

exit.reason: Terms not disclosed; Dropbox said the mobile experience would add to its smartphone and tablet efforts.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building tablet ad units and a collaboration workflow was ordinary web and mobile engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or network was described; ad formats and tools could be copied by larger ad platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dropbox acquired the team in July 2012, about a year after the batch, rather than any ad incumbent copying it.

market_need_then: Tablet adoption was growing fast in 2011 and rich media ad vendors such as Medialets reported higher engagement on iPad, but I found no direct evidence of customer spend on TapEngage itself.

branding.domain_note: tapengage.com now redirects to an unrelated company (Subsplash). The legal entity was Hactile, doing business as TapEngage, per a law firm announcement.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name resembles several tap-prefixed ad companies such as Tapad and Tapgage.

outcome_analysis: TapEngage was a two person tablet advertising startup from Summer 2011 that Dropbox bought in July 2012 for undisclosed terms, with the founders staying to work on next steps. No evidence of meaningful revenue or later rounds was found, and the one aggregator figure of 20 thousand dollars raised is unverified. The outcome looks like a talent and mobile experience acquisition, and founder Matt Holden had prior Dropbox and Google product roles.
notes: Unverified: one aggregator (CB Insights snippet) reports 20 thousand dollars total raised from Dropbox, Quotidian Ventures, TSVC and Y Combinator; no second source, so not recorded as a round. One M&A database dates the deal to 2013 which conflicts with TechCrunch (2012-07-17). The dated competitor search returned no TapEngage-specific results, so competitors are left empty. The company website now redirects to an unrelated firm. Completeness pass: the 20K total raised is recorded as one round of unknown date and stage from CB Insights, a single database; it may combine several investments.
